title: candidate-handoff-script-plus-week1-microlearning-path
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, conversational handoff script for recruiters and hiring managers plus a compact Week 1 microlearning path for new ICs. Goal: reduce first-week friction, standardize manager/buddy expectations, and surface micro-skills to measure during hiring and early onboarding.

When to use:
- After an offer is accepted and before the candidate’s first day.
- For IC hires across engineering, product, and platform teams where technical ramp is hands-on.

Audience:
- Recruiters completing the hire->team transition
- Hiring managers preparing a first-week plan
- Assigned buddy/mentor who will run shadow rotations

Quick summary script (recruiter -> hiring manager):
- Opening: “Congrats — we closed the candidate. Quick context: accepted offer, start date {start_date}, base comp and equity summary in Workday link. Candidate indicated top onboarding goals: hit dev environment by day 2, demo small feature by day 10.”
- Logistics handoff: “We verified equipment preference, relocation notes, and tax/visa flags. Onboarding ticket: HR-XXXX (link). New starter packet will hit their email 2 business days prior with ID and payroll steps.”
- Signal points: “They called out strengths in async collaboration, Git-based workflows, and debugging. Watch for ramp signals: independent PRs, timely triage responses, and ability to run full local test suite.”
- Ask of hiring manager: “Can you confirm buddy (name/email) and schedule 60-min kickoff on day 1? Also please add the new hire to team channel and give access to repo ABC by day 0.”
- Close: “I’ll assign follow-ups in the candidate record and ping you in Slack the day before start. Anything else you want tracked in the first-week plan?”

Manager -> Buddy quick script:
- Opening: “Thanks for being the buddy for {name}. Start date {start_date}. Goal is to get them to a reproducible local dev flow and one small merge by day 10.”
- Priorities: “Day 0/1 access checks, day 2 shadow pairing for core feature, day 3 write-first-PR checklist, day 5 independent small fix.”
- Handoff notes: “Known gotchas: mac M1 local test flakiness, tokenized infra access requires step X. I’ll unblock infra tickets but escalate early if provisioning slips.”

Immediate checklist (first 24 hours) — who owns each item:
- Welcome email + first-day agenda (people-ops)
- Equipment tracking and shipping confirmation (people-ops / IT)
- Invite to kickoff + 1:1 (hiring manager)
- Add to team Slack + relevant channels (hiring manager / buddy)
- Repo access + CI credentials (buddy / infra)
- Short “how-to-run-locally” doc pinned in PR template (buddy)
- Safety & compliance briefing scheduled (security/compliance)
content_2:
Week 1 microlearning path (modular, async-friendly):
Module A — Platform orientation (40–60m, day 0–1)
- Objective: know the topology (who owns infra, where logs live, how to open an incident).
- Deliverable: add one diagnostic note to the team runbook.
- Owner: buddy to assign materials and quick quiz.

Module B — Local dev and test flow (60–90m, day 1–2)
- Objective: get the app running and execute the full test suite locally.
- Deliverable: open a PR labeled "first-run" that updates a small README step.
- Support: pairing session with buddy (1.5h).

Module C — Read & review: codebase orientation map (30–45m, day 2)
- Objective: be able to point to the service owning core logic for the team’s primary product area.
- Deliverable: 5-minute whiteboard summary in team sync.

Module D — Incident triage primer (30–45m, day 3)
- Objective: recognize severity levels and who to ping.
- Deliverable: run a sandbox exercise (replay of a past P1) and submit one observation.

Module E — Product feedback loop (30–45m, day 4–5)
- Objective: make one product suggestion via PR or ticket with data-backed rationale.
- Deliverable: first backlog item or doc change proposed.

Timing model and completion signals:
- Micro-modules are 30–90 minutes each; ideally staggered with pairing slots.
- Completion = deliverable uploaded to onboarding tracker (a single checklist link). Buddy marks “module complete” in tracker.

Interview-rubric addendum (first-90-day micro-skills to surface during interviews and onboarding):
- Ownership tilt: look for examples where candidate moved a bug/feature from report to merged fix in under 2 weeks.
- Async clarity: evaluate an example of a PR description that communicated intent and testing steps.
- Debugging process: ask for a short post-mortem narrative (what they tried, how they confirmed the fix).
- Tooling fluency: confirm familiarity with the team’s primary CI and one observability tool.
- Communication under uncertainty: sample question: "You deploy and alert fires—how do you prioritize next five steps?" Capture bullet-style answers.

Manager / Buddy scoring quick sheet (use for early check-ins):
- Day 3 check-in (green/amber/red) across 3 dims: access, local-run, first-PR readiness.
- Day 10 check-in: independent PR + code review + written mini-summary.

Common friction hotlist & mitigations:
- Slow infra access: pre-provision staging accounts during offer acceptance window.
- Unclear first tasks: provide an explicit 2–4 hour "first contributor" ticket in the board with acceptance criteria.
- Overwhelming doc surfaces: curate a 1-page starter guide that links to canonical docs; buddy should own curation.

Notes & follow-ups:
- Recruiter: ensure offer packet contains links to onboarding tracker and buddy contact.
- People-ops: build the microlearning modules into LMS as short units (Q1 roadmap).
- Hiring manager: commit to scheduling 3 pairing sessions in week 1 and adding the new hire to a small, scoped work item by day 5.
